description: Pinned route-resolution replay cases. Each case bundles its own policy, synthetic environment snapshot, environment overrides, and fully pinned expected report, so one case can be read and replayed without opening another. Case order is DECLARATION order and is never sorted: an appended case must never reorder an existing one or perturb an existing case's pinned bytes. Agent names are synthetic and fixture- prefixed; no shipped agent name appears anywhere in this file. Every case's policy validates against route-policy.schema.json, its snapshot against environment-snapshot-projection.schema.json, and its expected_report against route-resolution-report.schema.json.

cases.purpose: An environment that no longer offers the preferred route's pinned resolved model, but does offer the declared fallback's.
cases.proves: The walk attempts the preferred route first, records it as rejected with a model_absent sub-reason, then selects the first compatible declared fallback and reports that fallback's tuple as the effective dispatch tuple.

diagnostics.message: Route preferred-primary pins a tuple the environment does not offer (model_absent).

remediation.summary: The route's pinned alias and resolved model no longer match the environment.
actions: Re-probe the environment and confirm the pinned alias and resolved model.

cases.purpose: An environment in which the preferred route names the real fable family alias, the alias still binds exactly as the route pins it, but the pinned resolved model is no longer offered — and the policy declares no fallback at all.
cases.proves: The fable-unavailable scenario the routing roadmap subordinates to preferred-model-absent lands on the model_absent sub-reason, and a preferred rejection over an empty fallback list leads directly to a report-only no-safe-route outcome carrying the verbatim rollback action.

cases.purpose: An environment whose alias-to-resolved-model table carries no binding at all for the preferred route's pinned alias, even though the model the route pins is itself offered.
cases.proves: An unbound alias is its own sub-reason rather than a fold into model_absent: the diagnostic names the alias and no model, because none was ever resolved. It also holds the evaluation order down — the pinned model IS available here, so a vocabulary that checked availability first would mis-report this input.

remediation.summary: The route's pinned alias and resolved model no longer match the environment.
actions: Re-probe the environment and confirm the pinned alias and resolved model.

cases.purpose: An environment whose alias table still binds the preferred route's alias, but to a resolved model other than the one the route pins — the shape provider-side version drift, per-family redefinition, and allowlist substitution all present as.
cases.proves: The diagnostic carries the pinned-versus-observed model pair, which is what distinguishes this sub-reason from the other three. The report also stays release_claim_eligible: the route that will dispatch is a declared qualified fallback whose model was present, and the route-scoped drift is carried by the rejected attempt entry and its sub-reason rather than by the report-scoped flag.

remediation.summary: The route's pinned alias and resolved model no longer match the environment.
actions: Re-probe the environment and confirm the pinned alias and resolved model.

cases.purpose: An environment that declares a platform-side route change against the preferred route's pinned tuple while leaving the binding wholly intact: the alias binds EXACTLY as the route pins it and the pinned resolved model IS among the available models.
cases.proves: The fourth sub-reason, reached only because the three alias-table predicates all miss. That construction is load-bearing rather than incidental — a snapshot that also repointed the alias would resolve to alias_repointed and one that omitted the model to model_absent, and because this report is pinned by hand either slip would surface as a replay failure whose stated cause looks unrelated to how the snapshot was built. It also shows the probe counter rising for a route this sub-reason rejects: the model is available and bound, so its probe state IS consulted.

diagnostics.message: Route preferred-route-changed pins a tuple the environment does not offer (platform_route_changed).

remediation.summary: The route's pinned alias and resolved model no longer match the environment.
actions: Re-probe the environment and confirm the pinned alias and resolved model.

cases.purpose: An environment offering the preferred route's model and binding its alias exactly as pinned, but supporting only the lower three rungs of the effort ladder while the route declares max.
cases.proves: Rejection at preflight, with the diagnostic naming BOTH the declared effort and the model's supported set. The divergence from documented runtime behaviour is deliberate and is pinned here: the runtime would silently degrade to the highest supported level at or below the declared one, and a route whose effort silently degrades is not the tuple the policy pinned. It also shows probe state still being consulted for a route an earlier check already rejected, since effort and probe support are independent grounds.

diagnostics.message: Route preferred-max-effort declares effort max, which model model-capped does not support.

remediation.summary: The route's declared effort is outside the model's supported effort set.
actions: Declare an effort the model's probed capability set supports.

cases.purpose: An environment marking capability probing for the preferred route's model with an explicit false rather than an absent key, and recording no exact-invocation outcome for it at all. This is where the frozen runtime-capability programme's undetermined observation lands.
cases.proves: Probe unavailability rejects the route, and probe absence is never read as probe success — an observation from which no availability claim derives is at least as weak as an absent probe, so treating it as selectable would be the substitution the requirement forbids. The absent exact-invocation outcome is not itself a probe failure, so exactly one diagnostic is emitted.

diagnostics.message: Route preferred-unprobed has capability probing unavailable for model model-unprobed.

remediation.summary: Capability probing is unavailable for the route's model.
actions: Re-run capability probing before trusting this route.

cases.purpose: An environment in which the preferred route's model is available, bound, effort-capable, and probe-available, but its exact-invocation probe outcome is a failure. This is where the frozen programme's hard_rejection observation lands.
cases.proves: An exact-invocation failure rejects the route and it is never selected: the route appears in the attempt list with disposition rejected and the walk continues to the next declared fallback.

diagnostics.message: Route preferred-probe-failure has an exact-invocation probe failure for model model-failing.

remediation.summary: The exact-invocation probe failed for the route's model.
actions: Inspect the exact-invocation probe evidence for this route.

cases.purpose: An undegraded environment: the preferred route's alias binds exactly as pinned, its model is offered, its declared effort is supported, capability probing is available, and its exact-invocation probe succeeds. A second qualified fallback is declared and never reached.
cases.proves: The clean-success path emits NO resolution diagnostic — an empty diagnostics array is a conforming report, which is why the array declares no minItems — while still recording the effective dispatch tuple, omitting unresolved_agent, and reading release_claim_eligible true. The unreached fallback also shows candidate_routes counting routes ENTERED rather than routes declared: the policy declares two and the walk enters one.

cases.purpose: A policy whose declared fallback chain names its own preferred route a second time, in an environment where every declared route's exact-invocation probe fails so the walk actually reaches the repeat.
cases.proves: The one policy-authoring violation decided against walk state rather than against the policy document. It is detected on REACHING the revisit, so the report carries the two routes attempted before it without repeating the revisited route, the revisited route is never consulted a second time, and the loop entry sits after the last attempted route's entries and before the terminal one. Reaching the repeat at all is why the environment degrades every route: a chain whose earlier route resolved would never get here, which is exactly why this code cannot join the pre-walk pass.

cases.purpose: A policy whose declared fallback names an adjacency to the qualified preferred route while not itself being qualified, against an environment that is wholly undegraded.
cases.proves: A defect of the policy DOCUMENT, decided before the first route is attempted. The adjacency is read from the route's own adjacent_to sibling reference rather than inferred from list position, the diagnostic names the declared route that was never attempted, and the walk is suppressed entirely: the attempt array is empty, all three counters are unspent, and the environment is excluded from release claims. The undegraded snapshot is load-bearing rather than incidental — the preferred route would have resolved cleanly, so nothing but the structural rejection can account for the outcome.

remediation.summary: The declared fallback is adjacent to a qualified route but is not qualified.
actions: Replace the adjacent model with a qualified route.

cases.purpose: A policy whose declared fallback dispatches a generic agent in place of the policy's own named synthetic agent, again against an undegraded environment.
cases.proves: The substitution is decided from the route's substituted_agent object whose class is generic, so the defect is a property of the declared document and not of the environment. The rejection is pre-walk on the same terms as the adjacency case: empty attempt array, unspent counters, and no effective dispatch tuple.

remediation.summary: The declared fallback substitutes a generic agent for the policy's named agent.
actions: Restore the named agent in the fallback route.

cases.purpose: A policy whose declared fallback omits BOTH its resolved model and its effort, so each would be materialized by inheritance rather than pinned by the policy.
cases.proves: The fixture the route contract must admit and the simulator must reject. Its policy validates against route-policy.schema.json — which is why resolved_model and effort stay optional there — and resolution rejects it pre-walk with one diagnostic naming the first omitted member. Requiring the members in the contract would fail this case at validation and no diagnostic would ever be produced, which is the inverted failure this pairing exists to prevent.

diagnostics.message: Route fallback-inheriting of policy fixture-required-executor omits resolved_model, which resolution would materialize by inheritance.

remediation.summary: The declared route leaves a dispatch member to be materialized by inheritance.
actions: Declare the model and effort explicitly on the route.

cases.purpose: An environment carrying a subagent-model override whose requested value binds to a model the organization allowlist PERMITS, over a policy whose preferred route resolves cleanly and matches the override on neither alias nor model.
cases.proves: The honored branch. The override becomes the effective dispatch tuple by its documented precedence, and that tuple is a HYBRID rather than a copy: the alias and resolved model come from the requested value while the agent and effort are retained from the route the qualified walk selected, because the variable sets a model only. The override is unqualified because its tuple matches no route the policy declares qualified, so the diagnostic is emitted at warning severity carrying no route-scoped join key, dispatch proceeds, and the consequence is carried by release_claim_eligible false. The would-have-been block records the qualified resolution the override displaced.

diagnostics.message: A CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL override requests alias-forced, which matches no route this policy declares qualified.

remediation.summary: An unqualified subagent-model override excludes this environment from release claims.
actions: Unset the unqualified subagent-model override before making release claims.

cases.purpose: The same subagent-model override value, against an environment whose organization allowlist EXCLUDES the model that value resolves to.
cases.proves: The allowlist-skip branch, and the bounded negative it is deliberately limited to. The override is skipped rather than honored, so the override record carries NO tuple: the documented fallback target is the inherited model, which this projection does not carry and must not gain, and naming any model there would assert one the simulation cannot know. The report's own effective dispatch tuple therefore follows the qualified walk. release_claim_eligible is false here too, for a reason independent of the override disqualifier. Without this second case the corpus would pin the unconditional override effect the documented runtime does not have.

diagnostics.message: A CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL override requests alias-forced, which matches no route this policy declares qualified.

remediation.summary: An unqualified subagent-model override excludes this environment from release claims.
actions: Unset the unqualified subagent-model override before making release claims.

cases.purpose: The one policy that declares an optional helper alongside its root required agent, in an environment that binds every alias but offers only the required agent's model — so both of the helper's declared routes name models the environment does not offer.
cases.proves: Both halves of the helper requirement. The helper is not consulted and the report records continuation on the validated no-helper path as a STRUCTURED field rather than as a diagnostic entry, with probe_attempts an explicit zero that makes the non-consultation measurable instead of self-asserted; that counter is disjoint from the agent's own, which stands at one. No attempted-route entry names a helper route, which is the corroborating structural evidence a counter alone cannot supply. And the second half: required-agent resolution does not fail as a result — the outcome is resolved, the tuple is the required agent's own route, and the environment stays eligible for release claims, so helper unavailability is not a disqualifier.

cases.purpose: An environment whose preferred route resolves to an available, probe-available model whose exact-invocation probe fails, under a policy declaring all three budgets at one while also declaring a fallback route that would have resolved.
cases.proves: Retry exhaustion specifically, which the roadmap states as its own proof obligation and which a probe-only case would leave unproven: the preferred route's exact-invocation outcome is a failure, the single permitted retry re-consults it and returns the same failure, and no further retry may be taken. Declaring the other two caps at one in the same case proves they are respected too — the walk truncates at max_candidate_routes rather than continuing to the declared fallback that would have resolved, so the cap is what produced the no-safe-route outcome. All three actual counts are pinned at their declared cap and none exceeds it, and details.exhausted_budget lists all three classes in the enum's declaration order, because with every cap reached no budget is causally privileged and no observable report content could settle which one terminated the walk.

cases.purpose: An environment that rejects the preferred route and both declared fallbacks on three different grounds — a re-pointed alias, an effort the model does not support, and capability probing unavailable — with every budget left well below its declared cap.
cases.proves: The report-only outcome in full. The report names the unresolved agent, records every attempted route with disposition rejected, and carries one diagnostic per failed check, each joined to the route it concerns by details.route_id — which is what makes 'each rejection reason' readable per route rather than as an unattributed list, since a variable number of diagnostics per route means the two arrays cannot be zipped by position. release_claim_eligible is false and the terminal no_safe_route entry closes the array at severity error, carrying the verbatim rollback action among its two actions while no per-route entry repeats it. Every counter ends below its cap, so details.exhausted_budget is omitted rather than emitted empty — the no-safe-route obligations attach to the outcome, not to budget exhaustion.
